Respectful, trauma-informed shared decisions: take her account of her symptoms seriously, explain each medicine and its reason plainly, write the plan down, and check costs with her before prescribing. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); Acute Myocardial Infarction in Women: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association (2016); Sex and Race/Ethnicity-Related Disparities in Care and Outcomes After Hospitalization for Coronary Artery Disease Among Older Adults (2016) [S]

Cardiology consultation on the day of the two-week visit, with an echocardiogram, to find the cause of the breathlessness, review the antiplatelet choice and the other medicines, and advise on rehabilitation and a return to the stage. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease and acute myocardial infarction monographs (2026) [S]

Dual antiplatelet therapy, aspirin 81 mg with a P2Y12 inhibitor, for twelve months from the heart attack, never stopped without speaking to cardiology; then aspirin alone. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease and acute myocardial infarction monographs (2026) [S]

Atorvastatin 80 mg daily; lipid panel four to eight weeks after the start; goal LDL below 70 mg/dL with at least a 50% fall; lipoprotein(a) measured once. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease and acute myocardial infarction monographs (2026) [S]

Metoprolol succinate for at least the first year after the heart attack; lisinopril for high blood pressure, with home readings and a target below 130/80 mmHg; potassium and creatinine one to two weeks after any dose change. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease and acute myocardial infarction monographs (2026) [S]

Enroll in a 36-session outpatient cardiac rehabilitation program, starting within two weeks, with exercise training, nutrition, stress management and psychological support; the clinic will call her if she misses sessions. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); Acute Myocardial Infarction in Women: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association (2016); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease and acute myocardial infarction monographs (2026) [S]

Depression after a heart attack: PHQ-2 and PHQ-9 today, repeat PHQ-9 at about twelve weeks, the rehabilitation program's psychologist, and a lower threshold for treatment if symptoms rise. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); Depression and Coronary Heart Disease: Recommendations for Screening, Referral, and Treatment: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association (2008); Depression as a Risk Factor for Poor Prognosis Among Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association (2014) [S]

Chest-pain action plan: nitroglycerin under the tongue, and 911 if pain is not better five minutes after the first tablet; warning symptoms in women, such as breathlessness, unusual tiredness, nausea or jaw, back or arm discomfort, explained. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); Acute Myocardial Infarction in Women: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association (2016) [S]

Costs: generic medicines in 90-day fills, the clinic social worker for debt advice and help with medicine costs, and rehabilitation sessions at times that fit her family. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023) [S]

Women's cardiovascular risk: record the hysterectomy of her thirties and a possible early menopause as a risk-enhancing factor; hormone therapy is not used to prevent heart disease. Guideline: Acute Myocardial Infarction in Women: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association (2016); Menopause Transition and Cardiovascular Disease Risk: Implications for Timing of Early Prevention: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association (2020) [S]
